title: The recorded pilots shift from logistics to strike work
observation: The competitive opening shows transport and building-supply work. Later the POV switches to rocket helicopters, and comms repeatedly assign enemy drills as priority targets.
interpretation: This air unit changes its contribution with available equipment and the scoring situation, rather than flying one role all game.
response: Expect the logistics pilot to become a strike threat later. Keep drill-warning and air-defence coverage active after the opening build phase.
limitation: This describes the recorded pilots and orders, not all TAB members or a measured damage total.

title: The command-to-air communications path fails visibly in comms
observation: Around 92 minutes pilots report no command whispers and identify a mute icon. At 120 minutes another whisper is not heard, followed by a request for warning before a drill pull.
interpretation: Separating pilot and squad channels can reduce chatter, but a failed cross-channel path leaves aircraft reacting late to the ground plan.
response: Time pressure when air is repositioning, but do not depend on a setup fault recurring. PHNT should verify a two-way command-to-air acknowledgement before the round and before important pulls.
limitation: The reports are explicit; exact missed orders and points lost cannot be reconstructed from this POV.

title: Indirect fire joins after the air unit is already struggling
observation: At about 122 minutes comms ask whether anyone is doing artillery. At 130 minutes artillery is tasked to remove rooftop AA. By 168 minutes the pilots credit it with opening the fight; Red rises from 35 at 130:00 to 68 at 170:00.
interpretation: The unit identifies a useful combined-arms dependency after repeated dangerous passes. The score recovery is consistent with broader improvement, but does not isolate artillery as the cause.
response: Establish indirect-fire ownership and a shared target mark before committing repeated air passes into an entrenched AA network.
limitation: Artillery is mainly off-camera. The pilots' praise is an assessment, not proof that earlier artillery would have won.

title: The air pair shares targets and coordinates approaches
observation: The paired-air sequence includes a common target, angle and pursuit calls, with repair/resupply between attempts. The pilots also request persistent pings for drill runs.
interpretation: A single isolated enemy aircraft or marked objective can draw a coordinated two-pilot response.
response: Avoid a prolonged isolated duel near both pilots. Cover the withdrawal and repair area while keeping objective AA ready for the returning pair.
limitation: Reported kills are not independently counted across the full match; pilot intent is clearer than every hit.

title: Converging on the same objective can break aircraft separation
observation: A Blue drill-response request around 175 minutes is followed by a collision at about 176 minutes. The sampled sequence returns to replacement equipment shortly afterward.
interpretation: The advantage of paired focus has a local execution cost when approach lanes and altitude are not separated.
response: Keep multiple threats active so the pair has to make fast hand-offs. In PHNT practice, assign lead/trail order, altitude and a clear pass-exit direction.
limitation: One collision is documented. The joking claim that it cost the game is explicitly rejected.

title: The finish shifts from asset hunting to immediate scoring presence
observation: Late comms prioritise drills and getting bodies into zone. Red recovers from 68 at 170:00 to 93 at 184:00, then finishes on 94 while Blue reaches 100.
interpretation: The air unit recognises that winning another dogfight is less valuable than reaching the decisive scoring area, but that change does not guarantee arrival in time.
response: Track the opponent's remaining scoring opportunity as well as the air fight. Keep one transport or ground route ready for the final contest.
limitation: The exact scoring mechanism and impact of airborne bodies are not derived from streamer assertions.

title: Entrenched rooftop anti-air forces a support response
observation: Pilots repeatedly report heavy Blue AA and dangerous repair/approach options. The artillery plan specifically targets the Blue rooftop positions before the air pair can get close.
interpretation: In this match, Blue's defended position shapes where and how the opposing aircraft can operate.
response: Scout the emplacement and supporting builders; coordinate indirect fire or another ground angle before repeatedly spending aircraft on the same approach.
limitation: The POV does not verify every emplacement, build legality, invulnerability claim or exact AA kill count.

title: Amnesty protects enough of its lead to finish the match
observation: Blue leads 67-40-16 at 140:00 and 86-68-39 at 170:00. Red closes to 95-93-39 at 184:00, but the final result is Blue 100, Red 94, Green 40.
interpretation: The comeback pressure does not prevent Blue converting the late scoring opportunity. A damaged base or reported lost drill does not mean the side has stopped scoring.
response: Keep direct awareness of the score and current scoring area after a successful asset strike; reserve a route to contest the next pull.
limitation: Outcome is direct; the enemy caller's decision sequence and each clan member's contribution are unknown.

title: Reported AA loss exposes a local harassment window
observation: Around 153 minutes the pilots report both Green AA positions down, then plan to repair, harass Green and potentially insert someone to steal the position.
interpretation: Once local anti-air is suppressed, the same defending area becomes a prospective insertion target.
response: Keep fallback AA, repair stock and an infantry guard ready while emplacements are rebuilt. Check whether the clearance is real before committing PHNT's own transport.
limitation: This is the pilots' local clearance report and follow-up intent, not proof all Green AA was absent or that the planned theft succeeded.
